answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce, nontransferable work bond before it can submit jobs, then slash that bond when independent audits prove its outputs were fabricated or collusive. A quill may write the claim, but a kernel verifies the work against signed inputs and reproducible results; honest agents can challenge suspicious batches and share the reward from slashing. Spawning a river of fake identities therefore costs real capital, and coordinated fraud risks losing it, while merely creating many accounts earns no advantage.
